title: Promises and challenges of generative artificial intelligence for human learning
extended_summary:
This perspective paper examines the role of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in human learning, asking how tools such as large language models and diffusion models may reshape teaching, learning, feedback, and assessment. Rather than reporting a single empirical study, the paper synthesizes literature across learning sciences, educational technology, and human-computer interaction to argue that GenAI has both major educational promise and serious risks.

The paper’s central “intervention” is the broad integration of GenAI into educational practice, including personalized tutoring, automated learning-resource generation, AI-generated feedback, and adaptive/authentic assessment. It discusses representative systems such as ChatGPT and Khanmigo, and uses examples from higher education, K-12, programming, writing, science, and assessment contexts to illustrate possible uses.

The authors conclude that GenAI can scale personalized support, diversify learning materials, provide timely feedback, and enable new forms of assessment, but only if its imperfections, ethical issues, and assessment disruptions are addressed. They emphasize the need for AI literacy, evidence-based decision-making, human-in-the-loop design, and stronger methodological rigor. Overall, the paper argues that GenAI should augment rather than replace human learning and teaching, and that future research must determine its real effects on cognition, metacognition, creativity, and learning outcomes across contexts.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed perspective article with no original empirical study, comparison, or causal evaluation. It synthesizes prior literature and offers recommendations, so it does not meet criteria for experimental or quasi-experimental evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: No direct student outcome is measured in this paper, so there is no empirical evidence of impact to rate. The article is about potential promises and challenges rather than demonstrated effects on K-12 achievement.

interventions.use_case: General-purpose generative AI tutoring and conversational support for learning, including ChatGPT/Khanmigo-style dialogic assistance, adaptive questioning, and personalized feedback in educational settings.
